full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-party Nos. 1-10 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 26-9-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 238 of 2009 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and order dated 4-10-2009 passed by the Additional Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Sadar, Chittagong in Misc. Case No. 2 of 2006 rejecting the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 decreeing the suit ex parte on 3-5-2006 should not be set-aside.

2. Facts necessary for the disposal of the Rule are that one Al-hajj Mahmuddunnabi Chowdhury, the predecessor of the defendant Nos.1-10 filed Other Class Suit No. 91 of 1990 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong for ejectment of tenant and realization of outstanding rent along with compensation against the defendant Sheikh Bashir Ali ( proprietor of M/s Mohammadi Metal Industry) and M/s Mohammadi Metal Industry. The suit was subsequently renumbered on transfer in the Court of the learned Additional Senior Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Sadar, Chittagong as Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995. During the pendency of the suit plaintiff Mahamuddun Nabi Chowdhury died and the opposite-party Nos. 1-10 were substituted as plaintiffs in place of their predecessor, Mahamuddun Nabi Chowdhury.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-2 entered appearance in the suit on 11-2-1991 and filed written statement on 19-5-1991 denying most of the allegations of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the defendant No. 1 is not a defaulter in payment of rent and the plaintiff filed the suit without serving any notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. The defendant Nos. 1-2, finally did not turn to contest the suit and consequently ex parte decree was passed on 3-5-2006.

4. In this background of the case the present petitioner showing himself 94 of 1995 as defendant of Other Suit No. 94 of 1995/90 of 1991 filed Miscellaneous case No. 2 of 2006 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte judgment and decree dated 3-5-2006 passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995/90 of 1991 stating that defendant Sheikh Bashir Ali converted his private enterprise Mohammadi Metal Industries into M/s Mohammadi Metal Industries Limited in 1981 and got it registered on 6-6-1991 as per Government registration No. C-9066/905 and the petitioner Salamat Hossain became its Managing Director and two other Share holders named Mrs Salma Begum and Habibur Rahman became Directors and afterwards M/S Mahammadi Metal Industries Limited expanded the Industry by including 5 other share holders named (1) Kazi Abu Kalam (2) Mrs Subra Das (3) Kazal Chandra Das (4) Md. Hashem (5) Abdul Hashem and after the death of Sheikh Basir Ali (Managing Director), the petitioner Salamat Hossain purchased the shares of Mrs Salma Begum and Md. Habibur Rahman on 28-11-2005 and thereafter, he became its Managing Director by a resolution of the general meeting of the Industry held on 20-12-2005 under section 110 of the company Act, 1994. The proceeding of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 was stayed by an order passed in Civil Revision 2231 of 1996 though after vacating said the order of stay the trial Court fixed. the suit for peremptory hearing on 3-5-2006 without notifying or informing the learned Advocate for the defendant Nos. 1-2 and the suit was decreed ex parte virtually against a dead man without impleading the successors of deceased defendant No. 1, Sheikh Basir Ali who died on 4-5-2003 and as such the ex parte decree is liable to be set-aside.

5. The plaintiff-opposite parties contested the Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2006 by filing written objection. The plaintiff-opposite parties case in short is that the petitioner Md Salmat Hossen was never a tenant of plaintiffs, nor the petitioner paid any rent to the plaintiffs nor there was any tenancy agreement between plaintiff/s and petitioner, Md Salamat Hossen nor the decree was passed against any dead man nor it is true that the trial of suit was resumed without informing to the learned Advocate of the principal defendants. The petitioner has no locus-standi to file the miscellaneous case under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree dated 3-5-2006 passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995/90 of 1991 and hence, the miscellaneous case is liable to be dismissed.

6. The trial Court by its judgment and order dated 4-10-2009 dismissed the Miscellaneous case No. 2 of 2006.

7. The unsuccessful petitioner Md Salamat Hossen then took an appeal therefrom to the Court of learned District Judge, Chittagong which was ultimately heard and disposed of by learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Chittagong who by his judgment and order dated 26-9-2010 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment of the trial Court and the instant Civil Revision is directed against that judgment and order dated 26-9-2010.

8. Mr Mohammad Jamir Uddin Sircar, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of both the Courts below and other materials on record submits that both the courts below having failed to consider that defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali, who died on 4-5-2003 and ex parte decree was passed on 3-5-2006 against deceased Sheikh Bashir Ali, which is a nullity and thus fell into an error of law in disallowing the Misc. Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the same has occasioned failure of justice. He next submits that the proceeding of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 was stayed by an order of this Court passed in Civil Revision 2231 of 1996 but after vacating the order of stay the trial Court fixed the suit for peremptory hearing on 3-5-2006 without notifying or informing the learned Advocate for the defendant Nos. 1-2 and in this way the suit was decreed ex parte virtually against a dead man without substituting the successors of deceased defendant No. 1, Sheikh Basir Ali who died on 4-5-2003 and, as such, at any rate the impugned ex parte decree dated 3-5-2006 is liable to be set-aside.

9. Mr Sircar further argues that both the Courts below failed to consider that the petitioner stepped into the shoes of Sheikh Bashir Ali, the Managing Director of M/s Mohammadi Metal Industries a private enterprise after it was transformed into M/s Mohammadi Metal Industries Ltd a public company and thereby most illegally arrived at a finding that the petitioner was not a party in Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 and the impugned ex parte decree was not passed against him and, as such, the same has occasioned failure of justice.

10. Mr Sk Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite-party Nos. 1-10, on the other hand, by filing counter affidavit supports the impugned judgments of 2(two) Courts below and contends that both the Courts below were perfectly justified in rejecting the petitioner's application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside ex parte decree dated 3-5-2006 on the clear findings that neither the petitioner, Md Salamat Hossain nor M/s Mohammadi Metal Industries Ltd. was defendant in the other suit No. 94 of 1995 and hence a third party is not entitled to file Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2006 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the decree passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995.

11. Mr Chowdhury next submits that original Other Suit No. 94 of 1995/90 of 1991 was decreed against Sheikh Bashir Ali, who was not in fact died on 4-5-2003 as alleged by the petitioner Md Salamat Hossen inasmuch as, it is apparent from the evidence of the petitioner Md Salamat Hossain in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2006 that he submitted annual report in the form of Particulars of Directors (PD) in the year 2005-2008 to the Registrar, Joint Stock Company and Firms showing the defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali as existing Director and alive, hence both the Courts below correctly found that the plea as raised by the petitioner that decree in question was passed against a dead man is not true. He adds that the petitioner Md Salamat Hossen did neither show nor produce any death certificate even on the date of filing of the instant revisional application from Khulna City Corporation or from any other authority showing that the defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali died on 3-5-2003 and subsequent death certificate dated 9-6-2007 allegedly issued by Khulna City Corporation filed by petitioner in his supplementary affidavit dated 7-2-2013 shows that the person Sk Bashir Ali named in said death certificate dated 9-6-2007 and the defendant No. 1 Sheikh Bashir Ali of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 are separate two persons but the petitioner Md Salamat Hossen for the first time at the belated stage with a view to fortify his case that defendant No. 1 Sheikh Bashir Ali of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 died at Khulna on 4-5-2003 produced a self manufactured death certificate before this Court.

12. Referring to the order sheets passed in other class suit No. 94 of 1995 Mr Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury submits that the contention as raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the judgment and decree was passed against a dead man is not correct inasmuch as, there is nothing on record to suggest that during the pendency of the suit the legal heirs or legal representative of defendant Nos. 1 and /brought the matter to the notice of the Court below that the defendant Sheikh Bashir Ali died during pendency of the suit rather the record speaks that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 after filing written statement willfully did not turn to contest the suit. Mr Chowdhury finally submits that from the finding of two Courts below and other materials on record it is evident that the petitioner as a illegal occupant in order to sit over the suit land years together without any payment of any rent filed this Misc. Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure with unclean and dirty hands and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged with exemplary cost.

13. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment, deposition of witnesses and other materials on record. The facts of the case have already been set out so, I need not to repeat the same again. Now, the material question for consideration is whether the Court of appeal below was justified in affirming the finding of the trial Court below that the petitioner has no locus-standi to file an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree dated 3-5-2006 passed in Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995.

14. In order to resolve this dispute let me advert the evidence on record. It appears that petitioner Md Salamat Hossain himself was examined as PW 1, who in his cross-examination categorically admitted that:—

“ মূল মামলার আরজিতে ছালামত হোসেন বাদী চিলেন ণা। --- মূল একতরফা ডিক্রী হওয়ার আগে আমি নিজে ওকালতনামা দস্তখত করে আমি কোন উকিল নিয়োগ করি নাই।  ------ মূল মামলায় আমি কোন জবাব দাখিল করি নাই। ------  মূল মামলায় আমি কোন জবাব দাখিল করি নাই। ------  প্রতিপক্ষগনের পূববর্তী মাহামুদুন্নবী মূল মামলা দায়ের করিয়াছিলেন বশির আলীর বিরুদ্ধে। মূল মামলার আরজীতে আমার বিরুদ্ধে কোন প্রতিকার চাওয়া হয়নি।  ------  সংশ্লিষ্ট সময় আমি মূল মামলায় ছিলাম না।”

15. From the above, it appears that the petitioner Md Salamat Hossain was not a defendant in original Other suit No. 94 of 1995/90 of 1991 nor there was any name in the plaint "Salamat Hossain" as defendant and no relief was sought for against him in the plaint  and he neither filed any vokalatnama nor appointed any Advocate to contest the suit. It is found that the Court of appeal below has come to the conclusion that the petitioner has no right to call in question the legality and propriety of the ex parte decree dated 3-5-2006 passed in Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 since he was not a party in the suit and no decree was passed against him. In coming to this conclusion the said Court has observed that the trial Court below on due consideration of the materials on record together with the case record of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 rightly arrived at a finding that the petitioner, Md. Salamat Hossain is a 3rd party, who has no locus-standi to file Misc. Case No. 2 of 2006 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995.

16. In view of the above finding of the Court of appeal bellow arrived at after considering the evidence on record, I do not find any possible reason to differ with the view taken by both the Courts below that in the facts and circumstance of the case the petitioner has no locus-standi to file Misc. Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree inasmuch as the petitioner was neither a party in the suit nor any decree was passed against him in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995.

17. To meet the submission of Mr Mohammad Jamir Uddin Sircar that the judgment and decree was in fact passed against a dead man which is a nullity, I have carefully examined the record, it appears that the principal defendant Sheikh Bashir Ali entered appearance in the suit and filed written statement on 10-5-1991 and lastly on 26-5-2005 after filing hajira he did not turn to contest the suit. It further appears that during pendency of the suit no one on behalf of the contesting principal defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali brought to the notice of the Court that the defendant Sheikh Bashir Ali died. Moreover, the petitioner to prove that during pendency of the suit Sheikh Bashir Ali died did not produce any death certificate of Sheikh Bashir Ali in the Courts below.

18. Further, it appears from the evidence of PW-1, petitioner Md Salamat Hossain that he  submitted annual report in the form of  Particulars of Directors (PD) in the year 2005-2008 to the Registrar, Joint Stock Company and Firms showing the defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali as existing director and alive, hence the plea as raised that the defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali died on 4-5-2003 appears to be false and without any legal basis. It also appears that the petitioner did not produce any death certificate of defendant No. 1 Sheikh Bashir Ali even on the date of filing of the instant revisional application from Khulna City Corporation or from any other authority showing that the defendant No. 1 Sheikh Bashir Ali died on 3-5-2003. It further appears from the plaint and decree in question that the address of Sheikh Bashir Ali had mentioned as 312/B, Love Lane, PS Kotwali, Chittagong but the death certificate shows the address of Sheikh Bashir Ali is written as 328, Sher-e-Bangla Road, Khulna (Annexure-B to the supplementary affidavit dated 7-2-2013) and thus, in the facts and circumstance of the case sitting under revisional jurisdiction it is very difficult to rely upon this type of death certificate. Therefore, I do not find any reason to hold that the petitioner has been able to prove that the ex parte decree was passed against a dead man.

19. Now, it remains for me to consider the last submission of Mr. Sircar that the petitioner stepped into the shoes of the original defendant Nos. 1-2 and in that view of the matter, it can not be said that the petitioner has no locus-standi to file Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995.

20. It appears that petitioner, Md Salamat Hossain as PW 1 categorically admitted in his evidence to the effect that "Defendant Mohammadi Metal Industries is proprietorship firm of Sheikh Bashir Ali and the Mohammadi Metal Industries Limited is not same establishment, both are different and separate establishment. Therefore, I am unable to see eye to eye to such submission of Mr Mohammad Jamir Uddin Sircar that the petitioner stepped into the shoes of defendant Nos. 1-2, rather I find there is a good deal of substance in the contention raised by Mr Sk Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury that the petitioner is a stranger to the suit, who has no right to file an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree passed in Other Suit No. 94 of 1995. It is on record that the principal defendant No. 1, Sheikh Bashir Ali after filing written statement finally did not contest the suit. Provision of Order XXII, rule 4(4) CPC provides that the heirs of non contesting defendant need not be substituted.

21. On perusal of the record, it appears that the proceeding of Other Class Suit No. 94 of 1995 was stayed by an order of this court passed in Civil Revision 2231 of 1996 and after vacating the order of stay the trial Court fixed the suit for peremptory hearing on 3-5-2006 which was seen by Mr Uma Pada Talukder, Advocate for the defendants before the hearing of the Other Suit No. 94 of 1995. So the allegation of passing decree beyond the knowledge of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 is not correct. The contentions raised for the aforesaid reason are of no substance.

22. By now I have covered all the points raised by Mr Mohammad Jamir Uddin Sircar.

23. On an analysis of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned Additional District Judge examined the records of the case and arrived at a finding inter alia, that: —

“ এমতাবস্থায় বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালত উপস্থাপিত সাক্ষ্য প্রমান ও অপর ৯৪/৯৫ মোকদ্দমার নথি পর্যালোচনাক্রমে প্রার্থী আপীলকারী অপর ৯৪/৯৫ মোকদ্দমার বিবাদীপক্ষ না হওয়ায় মিছ ২/০৬ মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করার আইনগত কোন অধিকার নাই মর্মে সিদ্ধান্ত প্রদান আইনসংগত হওয়ায় তর্কিত রায় বহাল থাকবে। প্রার্থী/আপীলকারীর আপীল মামলার দাবী এবং মিছ ২/০৬ মোকদ্দমার মিছ দরখাস্তের দাবী সম্পূর্নরুপে মিথ্যা ও মনগড়া হওয়ায় অত্র আপীল মোকদ্দমায় প্রার্থীত প্রতিকার পাবে না।”

<u>24. This findings of the Court of appeal below are in fact based on proper and correct appreciation of both law and fact. In view of provisions of law only the defendant of the suit can file Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of CPC with a prayer for setting-aside the ex parte decree. Stranger or any 3rd party has no locus-standi to institute or maintain Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside the ex parte decree passed.</u>

25. In view of my discussions made in the forgoing paragraphs it is by now clear that the instant Rule must fail.

26. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

Let a copy of this judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.

full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: These two appeals by the same parties, Appeal from Original Order No. 135 of 2008 directed against Order No. 162 dated 28-2-2008 and Order No. 163 dated 9-3-2008 and Appeal from Original Order No. 215 of 2008 arising out of Order No. 165 dated 19-3-2008 being related to the same auction sale in between the same parties are taken up together and this judgment would governed both these appeals.

2. The facts are not disputed City Bank Ltd obtained decree against Mobarak Re-rolling Mills Ltd. on 6-11-1993 and preliminary decree was made final on 15-10-1996. Execution Case No. 137 of 2003, renumbered as 6 of 1997, was filed before the Artha Rin Adalat on 31-5-2003 and the decreed property was sold in auction. The appellants, heirs of the original owners, who gave mortgaged the property, filed application under section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as per provision of Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This application was filed on 4-2-2008. Learned judge by Order No. 162 dated 28-2-2008 and Order No. 163 dated 9-3-2008 put this application for hearing on 19-3-2008 and said application having been disposed of by Order No. 165 dated 19-3-2008, as such, Appeal from Original Order No. 135 of 2008 stand as in fructuous.

3. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate to our utter surprise as this appeals arises out of orders passed by Artha Rin Adalat Ain, in his private capacity along with Mr Khan Saifur Rahman, Mr Abdul Quayum and Mr Sheikh Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, learned Advocates, appearing for the appellants submits that, the appellants being the heirs of the original mortgage have a right to protect their property and they offered to the bank to pay the decreetal amount which by board meeting No. 217 dated 12-11-1998 and the recommendation of the review committee and despite board meeting and recommendation of the review committee bank did not accept the proposal as well as the Court by the impugned order refused to act on these matters, as such, the order of the court suffer from legal infirmity and liable to be set-aside. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate, further submits, that section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 gave the Court ample jurisdiction to do justice where it requires, as such, when the heirs of the original owners wanted to maintain the property by paying the decreetal amount, this Court can exercise its jurisdiction and can pass necessary order for doing justice. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Advocate, further submits, that, the application under section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is to be considered applying provision of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure Court and court can pass necessary order to protect the interest of the applicant.

4. Mr Ahsanul Karim, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent on reference to section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 and also order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that, the application filed by the appellants is on misconception of law and fact as a decree can be set-aside at the instance of third party by a separate case, not on the same proceedings, as such, the application having been filed misconceived, should not be attended at all. Learned Advocate on reference to the letters given by the decree holder bank from 22-2-2009 till selling of the property, submits that, bank was always eager to settle the matter out of Court but the original borrower did not come forward to mitigate the matter out of Court when the execution of the decree was about to be barred by limitation, Bank put the decree into execution and thereafter sold the property, as such, on fact as well as on law the applicants have no case to be addressed to the Court.

5. Mr Omar Sadat with Mr Md Aminul Islam, learned Advocates, appearing for the auction purchaser respondent, submits that, this application filed by the applicants/appellants taking recourse to section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is not at all maintainable as the suit was filed in 1990 when Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 was prevailing, wherein there was no provision on of section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, as such, this application is totally misconceived one. Learned Advocates further submits that auction purchaser after purchase of the property, was inducted into possession and since then auction purchaser possesses the suit land and by this time auction purchaser improved the property by taking several development work the decree having been clearly executed and more so, the applicants/appellants have not proved they are the heirs of the original owners, as such, this application is not maintainable at all.

6. Mr Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appeared for respondent No. 4.

7. There are some admitted position in this appeal. Decree was put into execution on 27-2-1997 after preliminary decree was passed and final decree dated 15-10-1996, Appellant applicants earlier moved before this Court in Writ Petition No. 319 of 2008 and also some other legal proceedings under different law forum.

8. From the records it appears that the application was filed by the applicants not for setting-aside the decree but as follows: —

অতএব প্রার্থনা যে, ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে রায় ডিক্রীর মর্মানুযায়ী এর সিদ্দান্ত অনুযায়ী কিংবা রায় ডিক্রীতে বিজ্ঞ বিচারক আদালতের উপনীত সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে বিসিডি সার্কুলার অধীনে সুদ মওকুফ সুবিধার আওতায় কিংবা ডিক্রীদারের বোর্ড সভার ২১৭ তম সিদ্ধান্তের আলোকে শুরু হইতে শেষ পর্যন্ত হিসাব নিকাশ গ্রহন পূর্বক পরিশোধ যোগ্য দায় দেনা যদি বিজ্ঞ আদালত কর্তৃক নির্ধারিত হয়, তাহা পরিশোধ পূর্বক তপশীলোক্ত সম্পত্তি ডিক্রী ও বন্ধকী দায় হইতে অবমুক্তির জন্য এবং ১৩-১০-২০০২ ইংরেজী তারিখের যোগসাজশী প্রতারনাপূর্ন নিলাম ডিক্র্রী বাতিল করিতে প্রার্থীগনের অনুকুলে যথাযথ আদেশে প্রদানে বিজ্ঞ আদালতের সদয় আজ্ঞা হয়।

On a reading of the prayer portion of the application it appears that applicants did not want to set-aside the decree but want to modify the decree as per decision of the review committee as well as the decision of the board of the bank taken in board meeting No. 217. IN the second part of the prayer they made for setting-aside the decree as such first part of the prayer is totally contradictory to the second part of the prayer. It appears from the paper book that after the board meeting, bank on 22-2-1999, 3-2-1999 and 3-8-1999 requested the original mortgage to pay off the decreetal amount. And thereafter bank sold the property in auction. From letter dated 30-12-1999 it appears that original lessee was in know of the decree as well as the letters of the bank but original lessee gave a reason for not paying the decreetal amount.

গত ১২-১০-৯৮ ইং তারিখে দি সিটি ব্যাংক এর উর্দ্ধতন কর্মকর্তাদের সাথে আলাপ আলোচনার ভিত্তিতে একমত পোষন করে উক্ত ঋণ কমিয়ে সর্বযেটি ১০০,০০০০০ (এক কোটি) টাকা দেওয়ার সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহীত হয় এবং উক্ত সিদ্ধান্ত দি সিটি ব্যাংক বোর্ড মিটিংয়েও চুড়ান্তভাবে গৃহীত হয় ৷ আমি উক্ত সিদ্ধান্ত কে সম্মান প্রদর্শন করে ব্যক্তিগতভাবে গত ০২-১১-৯৯ ইং তারিখে জনতা ব্যাংক, মিরপুর-১ নং শাখার ইস্যুকৃত থে-অর্ডার নং… অ-১৫৫৮৯৩ এর মাধ্যমে দি সিটি ব্যাংকের চেয়ারম্যান জনাব আবুল হাসেম সাহেবের মাধ্যমে দি সিটি ব্যাংকের চেয়ারম্যান জনাব আবুল হাসেম সাহেবের মাধ্যমে ২০,০০,০০০ (বিশ লক্ষ) টাকা জমা করা হয় এবং ব্যাংকের বাকী পাওনা টাকার জন্য ২২-২-৯৯ ইং, ২-৩-৯৯ ইং ও ৮.৩.৯৯ ইং এ পর পর তিনটি তাগাদাপত্র পাঠান 1 তখন আমি পারিবারিক অসহযোগিতা ব্যক্ত করে ব্যক্তিগতভাবে উক্ত তাগাদা পত্রের জনাব হিসাবে ১৫-৩…৯৯ ইং তারিখে জনতা ব্যাংক কর্পোরেট শাখা, পুরানা পল্টন ঢাকা পে-অর্ডার নং-অ ১২৬৫০১০ এর মাধ্যমে ১,০০,০০০ (এক লক্ষ)টাকা জমা দিইঁ 1

সর্বোপরি উক্ত ঋণ পরিশোধ করার প্রবল ইচ্ছা থাকা সত্বেও পারিবারিক কলহ এবং জমা-জমি ভাগ বাটোয়ারা না হওয়ার জন্য ও ওয়ারিশগণের অসহযোগিতা, নানাভাবে হয়রানী এবং মস্তান বাহিনী কর্তৃক ভয়-ভীতি প্রদর্শন করার আমি ব্যবসা বাণিজ্য হতে বহু দূরে পড়ে আছি এবং কের ঋণের টাকা দিতে পারি নাই ৷যার ফলে ২৫-১০-১৯৯৮ ইং তারিখে আমাদের ঋণের বিপরীতে বন্ধকী সম্পত্তি ১ম বার নিলামে উঠে এবং সর্বোচ্চ ডাক হয় ২৮,১৫,০০০ (আটাশ লক্ষ পনের হাজার) টাকা ৷ তদাবন্থায় আমি আমার ব্যক্তিগত নামে পার্মেন্টস ফ্যাক্টরীর শেয়ার বিক্রি করে উল্লিখিত ২০,০০,০০০ (বিশ লক্ষ) টাকা প্রদান করার উক্ত দি সিটি ব্যাংক ১ম নিলাম ডাক স্থগিত করে এবং আমাকে সময়প্রদান করে ৷ পরবর্তীতে আমি আমার মৃতঃ ভাইয়ের ওয়ারিশগণের সাথে সালিশ করি ৷ কিন্তু তারা তাদের ভাগের ঋণের টাকা না দেওয়ার ব্যাত্কের দেয়া সময়ে ঋণ পরিশোধ করিতে ব্যর্থ হই এবং উক্ত সম্পত্তি আবারও ২য় বারের মত নিলামে উঠে; যার তারিখ ছিল ১১-৮-৯৯ ইং ৷ কিন্তু আমার অক্লান্ত পরিশ্রমে গড়ে উঠা শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠানটির মায়া ছাড়িতে পারি নাই বলে আমি আবার আমার ব্যক্তিগত স্থাবর সম্পত্তি বিক্রি করে জনতা ব্যাংক মিরপুর শাখার ইস্যুকৃত ডি ডি নং ৩৩৯২৮৫৯/৩৩, তারিখ ১-৯-৯৯ ইং এর মাধ্যমে ১০,৫০,০০০ (দশ লক্ষ পঞ্চাশ হাজার) টাকা ও চেক, যাহার নং-সি এ/এ আই বি ০১২৯৮১, তারিখ ৫/৯/৯৯ ইং এর মাধ্যমে ৩,০০,০০০ (তিন লক্ষ) টাকা ব্যক্তিগতভাবে দি সিটি ব্যাংকে প্রদান করি ৷ ফলে ব্যাংক ২য় নিলামও বাতিল করে ৷ আমি উক্ত টাকা জমা দেওয়ার পূর্বে এম,ডি, সাহেবের সাথে দেখা করি তখন উনি আমাকে জনাব মনিরুজ্জামান খন্দকার সাহেবের সাথে আলোচনা করার কথা বলেন, আমি উনার কথামত আলাপ করে চট্রগ্রাম শাখায ১৩,৫০,০০০ (তের লক্ষ পঞ্চাশ হাজার) টাকা জমা দেই। তখন উনি আমাকে বলেন যে, বাকী টাকা ৩১ শে ডিসেম্বর ১৯৯৯ ইং এর মধ্যে জমা দিতে হবে। আমিও সেই মত প্রস্তুত হতে থাকি। কিন্তু দুঃখের বিষয় এই যে, গত ৮-১১-৯৯ ইং তারিখে তৃতীয় বারের মত নিলামে উঠে।

9. Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure runs as follows:—

"90. (1) Where any immoveable property has been sold in execution of a decree, the decree-holder, or any person entitled to share in a ratable distribution of asserts, or whose interests are affected by the sale, may apply to the Court to set-aside the sale on the ground of a material irregularity or fraud in publishing or conducting it;

Provided that no sale shall be set-aside on the ground of irregularity or fraud unless upon the facts proved the Court is satisfied that the applicant has sustained substantial injury by reason of such irregularity or fraud."

10. On a reading of this law a decree or a sale or property sold in auction can be set-aside whether fact alleged smelt fraud. In the case of Ahmed Miah vs Ejahar Miah, 40 DLR (AD) 26 it is held that when application failed to prove that to because of fraud, he could not filed the application within time or the applicant must prove he from the date of knowledge of such fraud filed the application within time committed no illegality in rejecting application. From the aforesaid factual aspects particularly the correspondence in between original mortgage and Bank it can safely be said these was no fraud in auction selling the property on 8-11-99.

11. From the aforesaid fact it is clear that disputed property was sold within the knowledge of owner of the property. It is argued that appellants are descendent from daughter. It appears that Mobarak ullah died leaving two sons and a daughter. Suit was filed on and it was decreed on 30-10-1993. Execution case was field on 27-2-1997 and it was duly executed on 8-11-1999. Applicants as we see, first on the scenario in 2008 when petitioners one of them is grand son-in-law of original owner when they filed the writ petition No. 319 of 2008. Thereafter, several litigation were taken in fatality before Court below and before this court from all these litigation it appears that petitioners are bent upon to frustrate the decree.

12. When the suit was filed Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990 possessed no provision as like section 57 of 2003. Section 32 of Artha Rin Adalat AM provides to follow procedure as in Civil Procedure Code, Civil Rules and Orders in chapter Miscellaneous Judicial Cases in rule. 774 provides for miscellaneous judicial cases under Order XXI Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure but we do not find appellants filed any such cases.

<u>13. The appellant  filed their application dated 4-2-2008 for setting-aside the sale under section 57 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Such application under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain is not maintainable. Section 57 of the said Ain confirms the inherent power of the court. Section 57 of the said Ain is not any enabling provision for setting-aside of sale. Section 57 of the said Ain reiterates the provision of section 151 of CPC, which just confirms the inherent power of court. Inherent power of the court cannot be exercise when there is specific provision in CPC and other law. There is provision for setting aside Sale under CPC such as Order XXI Rule 90 of CPC. Section 32 of the said AM a 3rd party can file any clairri against any order of the Artha Rin Execution Court only in the manner allowed under CPC. The appellants were not party in the suit, neither were made party in the execution case. So the present appellants filed their application dated 4-2-2008 as 3rd party in the said execution case for setting-aside the sale. But the present appellant did not file the said application under any provision of CPC. Therefore, their application for setting-aside for sale under inherent power of the said execution court is not maintainable when there is alternative remedy. The appellants could have availed the provision of Order XXI Rule 90 or could have filed separate suit. There is alternative remedy under the court for setting-aside the sale. So the said application dated 4-2-2008 of the appellants not being maintainable the instant appeals are also not maintainable.</u>

<u>14. The decree holder bank filed Mortgage Suit No. 138 of 1991 on 1-12-1991 before the 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong. The said 1st Artha Rin Adalat passed judgment in the said mortgage suit on 30-10-1993. Pursuant to the said judgment dated 30-10-1993, the said 1st Arena Rin Adalat, Chittagong had drawn preliminary decree in the said mortgage suit on 06-11-1993. Thereafter, the said 1st Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong had drawn final decree on 15-10-1996. The decree holder bank having obtained final decree on 15-10-1996 filed execution Case No. 6 of 1997 (Re-numbered as Artha Rin Execution Case No. 137 of 2003) before the 1st Court of Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong on 31-5-2003. The decree holder bank filed the said Execution Case against final decree as drawn on 15-10-1996, not against the preliminary decree as drawn on 6-11-1993. The mortgage property was sold in the said execution case 13-10-2002 vide order No. 101 dated 13-10-2002 of the said. Execution Court. Thereafter, the auction purchaser deposited rest of the auction money and the execution court fixed 13-11-2002 for confirmation of auction sale. Thereafter, the said Execution Court vide order No. 110 dated 3-11-2002 confirm the auction sale and made the said sale absolute. Now the appellants filed an application dated 4-2-2008 before the execution Court for setting-aside the said sale on the ground that the execution court did not consider decision of one review Committee as referred to a preliminary decree. It is submitted that as has been stated above, the decree holder has filed the said execution case for executing the final decree dated 15-10-1996 not the preliminary decree dated 6-11-1993, but in the final decree there is no reference of Review Committee or any one else, neither is there any direction to take consideration into any decision of any Review Committee or any other authority or person. It is settle principle that the execution court cannot go behind the decree. So the execution court does not have any jurisdiction to take into consideration of any thing stated in preliminary decree.</u>

15. The appellants filed their application for setting-aside the sale of the mortgage property. But as has been stated above the said mortgage property sold out to 3rd party auction purchaser on 13-10-2002 and the auction sale was made absolute by way of confirmation on 13-11-2002. It is settle principle of law the sale of the property once made absolute the same is not affected even if the decree is reversed. The sale can be set-aside under provisions laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 on the grounds provided in the said provisions. In the instant case the judgment debtors once filed an application under Order XXI Rule 90 of the CPC. The execution court vide order No. 150 dated 15-3-2004 rejected the said application of the judgment debtors after giving detailed reasoning. The present appellants have not filed any proper application under Order XXI Rule 90 for setting-aside the sale. The present appellant has filed the said application dated 4-2-2008 under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. Therefore, there being no application for setting-aside the sale under the permitted provisions of CPC and the Artha Run Adalat Ain, 2003, the instant appeals have no merit.

16. As has been submitted before, the final decree was drawn on 15-10-1996 and sale pursuant to the said final decree was confirmed on 13-11-2002. The present appellants has been arguing before this Hon'ble court that they have right of equitable redemption. But it is settle principle of law that after drawing final decree the right of redemption of the mortgagor does survive any more. After final decree the mortgagor has only remedy under Order XXXIV Rule 5 of CPC. But such remedy under order XXXIV Rule 5 of CPC can be availed of only before the sale pursuant to the said final decree is confirmed by the court. Therefore, the sale being confirmed by the court and 3rd party interest having accrued the appellants cannot have any right to redemption.

<u>17. Appellants were not defendants in Mortgage Suit No. 138 of 1991. Neither were they party in the execution case. The appellants are allegedly heirs of one late Umme Kulsum Chowdhury, who was allegedly daughter of late Mobarak Ullah Chowdhury, the mortgagor. The appellants not being party in the said execution case are third party so far sale of mortgage property in the said Execution Case is concerned. The execution court confirmed sale on the said execution Case is concerned. The execution court confirmed sale on 13-11-2002. Thereafter, the appellants after more than 5 years on 4-2-2008 field an application in the said Artha Rin Execution Case No. 13 of 2003 for setting-aside the sale of the said mortgage property. This instant appeal has been arisen out of the rejection of the said application dated 4-2-2008 by the Execution Court. The Execution Court vide order No 164 dated 19-3-2008 rejected the said application for setting-aside the sale. The appellants filed the said application as third party for setting-aside the mortgage sale. But under section 32 of the said Ain such application can only be maintainable if the third party deposits security to the tune of Taka 25% of the decretal amount. The appellant did not deposit any security at the time of filing of the said application is not an application in the eye of law in absence of security as required under section 32 of the said Act. Therefore, the said application is not maintainable and the execution Court rightly rejected the said application for setting-aside the mortgage property in absence of required security. The requirement of depositing 25% of decreetal amount is mandatory since the consequence of not depositing 25% of decreetal amount is stipulated in the said section 32 of the said Act to the effect that the said application shall be rejected. So the execution court rightly rejected the application of the appellants and hence the instant appeals are liable to be dismissed.</u>

18. Considering all these aspect of the case we are of the view that application filed by the applicants/appellants are totally misconceived and since the applicants/appellants did not produce any thing before the learned judge, as, Mr Sheikh Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, learned Advocate submits that applicants were not given a chance to bring the record or Exhibited this document, we are of the view that there is no supporting documents in favour of the applicants and the appeals have no merit and liable to be dismissed.

19. Various decisions cited by both the appellants as well as defendants but since the application filed misconceived we are not required to go deep into merit of these decisions but if the applicants/appellants so advised, they can take legal forum as per provision of law and can agitated their grievance in that forum. A question may be arise on limitation which is mixed question of law and fact and since this application filed on misconception of law or Court is exempted the provision of section 29 of the limitation Act.

20. Money deposited as per order of this Court by the applicants/appellants, the applicants/appellants are liberty to withdrawal the money if they want.

21. In the result, both these appeals i.e. First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 135 of 2008 with First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 215 of 2008 are dismissed with these observation.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.

Md. Moinul Islam Chowdhury J: Supplementary affidavits filed by the petitioner be formed part of the main petition.

2. At the instance of the petitioner, Mrs. Dilruba Morshed, this Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned order No. 42 dated 07 October 2008 passed by the Respondent No. 1, in the Artha Miscellaneous Case No. 21 of 2008 arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 Artha Zari Case No. 153 of 2007 rejecting the application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (Annexure-F) for setting aside the exparte decree should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

3. The relevant facts for disposal of this Rule are that the respondents No. 02 and 03, Mercantile Bank Limited and its the Branch office as plaintiffs instituted the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 in the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Chittagong, for realisation of Tk. 53,15,235.76 (Fifty three lakh fifteen thousand two hundred thirty five and paisa seventy six) impleading this petitioner as defendant alleging inter-alia that the defendant No. 1, M/s Nafico International, has been carrying on a business, the defendant No.2 is the proprietor of the Defendant No.1. The Defendants Nos. 3-8 mortgaged their properties through their attorney in favour of the defendant No. 1 (the present respondent No. 2) for a composite limit facilities in the form of Letter of Credit (Cash) and LTR for Tk. 2,50,00,000 (two crore fifty lakhs) and Cash Credit (Hypo) loan for Tk. 50,000,00 (fifty lakhs) which was sanctioned on 2-11-2000 by the bank. The present Respondent nos. Alhaj Md. Saidur Rahman (the defendant No.2 in the suit) on behalf of the present petitioner and other mortgagors executed charge documents as a constituted Attorney of all mortgagors but the present respondent No.5 failed to repay the dues within the granted period.

4. Later on, after serving several notices the present petitioner and the respondent No.5 to 10 deposited Taka 30, 00, 000 (thirty lakh) on 15-4-2005 towards the original loan amount plus interest thereon. Despite several requests the present petitioner and the respondents failed to deposit the remaining amount of Taka 53,15, 235.76 (Fifty three lakh fifteen thousand two hundred thirty five Taka and seventy six paisa) as on 31-8-2006. For realization of the said remaining money, the present respondent No. 2 and 3 filed the Suit No.66 of 2006 which was decreed exparte on 20-6-2007. The respondent Nos. 2 and 3 as plaintiff decree holder-bank instituted the Artha Rin Jari Case No. 153 of 2007 in the Court of Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong for execution of decree. The respondent No. 1, the Adalat, through the Court procedure sold in auction the schedule properties of the defendant judgment-debtors, the present petitioner by its order No. 18 dated 22-5-2008 on consideration of Taka 1,73, 22, 000, even though, the present price of the property owned by petitioner (scheduled 6 of the plaint of the Artha Rin Suit) was claimed to be more than Tk. 2 crores.

5. It is further stated that even though the petitioner was a defendant in the said Artha Rin Suit filed by the present respondent Nos. 2 and 3 but no notice was served upon the petitioner. After knowing about the said exparte decree the present petitioner filed the Artha Misc Case No. 21 of 2008 on 25-9-2008 under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 alleging that the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 bank by filing the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 against the mortgagors got an exparte decree without serving any notice upon the petitioner. The petitioner came to know about the said exparte decree for the first time on 18-9-2008. The petitioner as a third party mortgas or expressed her readyness through the Misc Case No. 21 of 2008 that she was ready to pay 10% of the decreetal dues and thereby prayed to set aside the exparte decree. After hearing the parties the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagnog, the respondent No. 1, by its order No. 42 dated 7-10-2008 was pleased to reject the application filed under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003.

6. Challenging the said order passed by the Adalat the petitioner invoked this writ jurisdiction and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. Shah Md. Munir Sharif, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits before us that the respondent No. 2 and 3 bank filed the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 on 07-9-2007 impleading the petitioner as respondent No. 8 but suppressing the Sumons upon the petitioner the Bank got an exparte decree on 20-6-2007 and the petitioner came to know about the decree on 1 8-9-2008 where by she filed the Misc Case No. 21 of 2008 under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 on 25-9-2008 wherein she expressed her readiness to pay 10% of the decreetal dues and in fact produced a pay order in the Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong for an amount of Tk. 5,31,523.85 but the Adalat by the impugned order dated 07-10-2008 rejected the application for setting aside the exparte decree without lawful authority

8. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that even though the exparte decree was passed on 20-6-2007 in the Artha Rin Suit No.66 of 2006 and the Artha Jari Case No. 153 of 2007 were filed but the petitioner had no knowledge of those proceedings therefore the petitioner could not under-take any step until 18-9-2008 but by the impugned order the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong passed in Artha Misc Case. No. 21 of 2008 wrongly quoted the names of the two daily newspapers namely "Dainik Ittefaque and Daily Naya Diganta" purported to show a publication of auction sale notices because there were no publication of notices through the afore named two newspapers, therefore, mistakenly concluded as to the notices required under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain for an auction sale of a mortgaged property, as such the impugned order by itself is an error apparent on the face of it, therefore, the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority.

9. In support of the above contention the learned Advocate referred a case of Farid Uddin Mahmud vs Md Saidur Rahman as reported in 66 DLR (AD) 93 wherein their Lordships of our apex Court found in the following terms:

"A writ of certiorari may issue in exceptional cases. where the proceedings of the Tribunal are absolutely void or where the Tribunal has purported to act in a judicial capacity which is not properly constituted or where there is error apparent on the face of the record or where the Tribunal's conclusion is based on no evidence on record whatsoever, or where the decision of the Tribunal is vitiated by mala fide, or the Tribunal has acted without jurisdiction or acted in excess of jurisdiction or acted contrary to the fundamental principles or acted malice in law, interfere is called for. In the absence of the above grounds, the Court will not interfere however erroneous or improper it may be."

10. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also submits before us that the impugned order mentioned about publication of auction notices through "Dainik Ittefaque and new Dainik Naya Diganta" but in fact the respondent bank published the auction notices only in the local newspapers, namely, Dainik Samokal, Dainik Ajker Chattagram, which is a clear violation of the provisions of sub section (i) of .section 7 of the Ain wherein it was required by the bank to publish an auction notice in “একটি বহুল প্রচারিত বাংলা জাতীয় পত্রিকা এবং একটি স্থানীয় পত্রিকা” therefore it was not sufficient for service of notice upon the debtors on default to repay the borrowed money, as such it is a clear violation of the provisions of Ain therefore it should be declared without lawful authority. In support of his aforesaid contention the learned Advocate cited a case of Sonali Bank Limited vs Prime Global Limited as reported in 63 DLR (AD) 99. The learned Advocate for the petitioner particularly drawn our attention to paragraph 13 which reads as follows:

"Besides, the learned Judges should be careful that the publication of the summons through the national newspapers should be in one of the top 10 (ten) newspapers which has got the highest circulation in the country. The figure of circulation can very well be obtained from the Publication and Information Department (PID) of the Government. These steps would ensure due diligence in the service of summons from the office of the Court upon the defendants."

11. On the basis of the above submission the learned Advocate for the petitioner prayed to make the Rule absolute.

12. Rule has been opposed by the respondent No. 11. Mr. Farid Uddin Mahmud, the auction purchaser through a proceeding undertaken by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong in Artha Jan Case No. 153 of 2007 contending inter alia that the required notice and Summons were duly served upon all the defendants of the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 in accordance with law and the defendant No.1 and 2 in the Artha Rin Suit Messers Nafico International and Md. Saidur Rahman filed a written statement in the said Suit.

13. It is further alleged that Mr. Saidur Rahman has been a constituted Attorney through a registered power of Attorney of the present petitioner, Dilruba Morshed being the registered deed Na 5923 dated 10-10-2000 and the petitioner mortgaged her property through the said Attorney, empowering to sell, mortgage etc. therefore required provisions under sub section (2) of section 19 knowledge (অবগতি)was sufficiently satisfied as to the decree passed exparte by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong on 20-6-2007, as such, the petitioner's knowledge of the exparte decree on 18-9-2008 is not true and therefore denied. The affidavit-in-opposition and also the supplementary affidavit in-opposition further alleged that from the order sheet of the learned Adalat, it is clear that notices as required under the provision of the Ain, 2003 were sent by post and also published in the daily newspapers.

14. It is also stated that the present respondent Nos. 5 to 10 filed several writ petitions in the High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court to stop auction sale, therefore, regarding the finding of the learned Adalat by the impugned order there is no arbitrariness or misapplication of Judicious mind in passing the impugned order on 07-10-2008. The affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 11 further contends that the certified copies of the plaint of the Artha Rin Suit No. 66 of 2006 which has been annexed by the petitioner as (Annexure A) of this writ petition clearly shows that an application or applications were made by the petitioner and/or her Attorney for obtaining certified copies on 07-7-2008 and the certified copy was made ready on 09-7-2008 but the same was delivered on 01-9-2008 therefore the alleged dated of knowledge dated 18-9-2008 as claimed by the present petitioner is false statement made by the petitioner.

15. It is stated that on the basis of the above circumstances, the learned Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Chittagong ,made no mistake disbelieving the statement made by the petitioner in the Misc Case No. 21 of 2008, therefore, no illegality has been committed by the learned Adalat rejecting the application by the impugned order dated 07.10.2008. It is further contended in the affidavit in opposition that the principal borrower Md. Saidur Rahman was the constituted Attorney as well as the brother-in-law (Husband of the petitioner's full Sister) and other mortgagors, including her full Sister and who are also relative of the petitioner and who are loanees under the law and others who filed several writ petitions being Nos. 6552 of 2006, Writ Petitions No. 1720 of 2008 and Writ Petition No. 3684 of 2008 in order to frustrate the procedure under-taken for serving the auction notices and for also the finality of the auction sale to the present respondent No. 11.

16. It is also contended that on 14-6-2006 the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 bank published an advertisement for auction sale of the mortgaged property under section 12 sub section (3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in the National newspaper, known as, "Dainik Prothom Alo" on 12-2-2008 an auction notice was published auction sale in the national newspaper of "Dainik Ittefaque" and local newspaper of "Dainik Bir Chattagram Mancho" and challenging the said publications of auction sale the present respondent No.5, Md. Saidur Rahman, the judgment debtor No. 2 filed a Writ Petition No. 1720 of 2008. The bank yet again published an auction sale notice in National Dainik Samokal on 10-5-2008 and National Daily Naya Diganta on 11-5-2008 through the process of Court. By the order No.18 dated 22-5-2008. The mortgaged landed property was sold in auction to the present respondent No. 11, the auction purchaser, Farid Uddin Mahmud, at a price of Tk. 1,73, 22,000 and deposited 10% of it by a pay order. Thereafter the said Md. Saidur Rahman filed Writ Petition No. 3684 of 2008 and Writ Petition No. 5585 of 2008 in the High Court Division regarding the auction sale through the process of Court. It is also stated that by an order No. 29 dated 20-8-2008 the auction sale was confirmed by depositing the balance auction amount. Subsequently, under order 21 Rule 94 of the Code of Civil Procedure the sale Certificate was issued and the sale deed being No. 16355 dated 29-10-2010 was executed and registered. Therefore, the respondent No. 1, Farid Udden Mahmud, got and acquired an absolute ownership of the landed property in question, therefore, the application in the Misc Case No. 21 of 2008 filed under section 19 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 made by the petitioner with a mala fide intention and in order to frustrate the auction sale, as such, the impugned order passed by the learned Adalat is on the basis of the record in front of him.

17. Mr. Mahabubey Alam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing in personal capacity along with Mr. Sk. Rezaul Haque, the learned Advocate submits before us that throughout the procedure in Artha Rin Suit and the Artha Jari Case filed by the present respondent No. 2 and 3 the Mercantile Bank Limited served the required notices upon the borrower defendants of the Suit including the present petitioner. Drawing our attention to the order sheet of the Suit he submits that these notices were served with registered posts and thereafter notices were published in the National Daily Newspapers regarding the sale of the property in auction and thereby the requirements of the provisions of the, Artha Rin Adalat Ain have been satisfied, therefore, an application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain filed on the plea of knowledge as to the exparte decree passed on 20-6-2007 is a mere dilatory tactice in the procedure of the Court even though a valid transfer of the property has been completed in the favour of the respondent No. 11, as such, the impugned order passed on 07-10-2008 was passed within the frame work of the law, thus, the present writ petition is liable to be discharged.

18. The learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 11 further submits that from the documents filed by the petitioner clearly show that the present petitioner had knowledge of the exparte decree prior to a fictitious date of 18-9-2008 and the application under section 19 is not a bona fide application, and the learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong passed the impugned order disbelieving the petitioner's prayer in relation to the knowledge of the exparte decree on the basis of the publications in the "Daily Ittefaq and Naya Diganta" therefore the learned judge made no mistake as to the requirements of law under section 19 sub section (2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, as such he submitted to discharge the Rule.

19. The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent No. 11 further submits that the present petitioner is a party to the original Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 66 of 2006 and also the subsequent Execution Case being Artha Rin Execution No. 15 3 of 2007 who had an efficacious remedy of filing an appeal against any order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat under section 41 of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 therefore, this writ petition is not maintainable and the same is liable to be discharged.

20. In support of his aforesaid argument the learned Senior Advocate cited a case of Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) vs Artha Rin Adalat as reported in 59 DLR (AD) 6 reads as follows:

"In view of the decisions quoted above are led to irresistible conclusion that there being specific remedy in the statute for filing appeal against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat in the present case the defendant not availing of the aforesaid remedy cannot maintain the writ petitions. Since we find that the writ petitions were not maintainable we do not like to embark upon other submissions made on behalf of the defendant petitioner touching the merits of the cases."

21. On the basis of the above submissions, the learned Senior Advocate prayed to discharge this Rule.

22. Having considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates appearing for the parties and also perusing the writ petition and the annexures therein and also the Supplementary Affidavits filed on behalf of the petitioner and the affidavit-in opposition and annexures therein, it appears to us that the present respondent No. 3, Mercantile Bank Limited, Agrabad Branch under the district of Chittagong sanctioned a composite Limit in the form of Letter of Credit (Cash) LTR and Cash Credit (Hypo) for Tk. 250 crore and Cash credit (Hypo) Limit for 50,00,000 (Fifty Iakh) on 02-11-2000 in favour of the present respondent Nos. 4 and 5 defendants enjoyed the aforesaid loan facilities by executing charge documents by the present respondent No. 5 (the defendant No. 2 in the Artha Rin Suit) and the present respondent Nos. 6, 7, 8, 9 and the present petition defendant Nos. 2 to 8 of the Suit) executed personal guarantee through their Attorney by mortgaging their personal properties, (Schedule-B), in favour of the plaintiff, the present respondent No. 3 Bank.

23. It also appears that the present petitioner, Mrs. Dilruba Morshed executed a registered Special Power of Attorney on 10-10-2000 in favour of the present respondent No. 5, Alhaj Saidur Rahman, who executed a mortgage deed being No. 6652 of 2006 on 05.11.2000 and also executed an irrevocable general power of attorney for selling the mortgaged property in case of default in payment of the borrowed money. It further appears from Annexure-6 of the Supplementary Affidavit-in-opposition that the present petitioner executed a Power of Attorney in favour of the present respondent No. 5 on 10-10-2000 vesting powers to act on her behalf for the purposes by the registered deed No. 5923 dated 10-10-2000 for selling, mortgaging, transferring etc. her property as mentioned in the schedule of the said Deed of Power of Attorney. On the basis of the aforesaid power of attorney Mr. Saidur Rahman executed the aforesaid mentioned deeds in favour of the bank. When principal borrowed the respondent No.5 and other borrower failed to repay the loan amount within the stipulated time the petitioner as a mortgagor along with others because defaulters under the law. The present respondent Nos. 2 and 3 undertook the necessary proceeding under the provisions of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 including, publishing notices for auction sale of the scheduled properties owned by the present petitioner and the respondent No. 5 to 10 of the present writ petition. It appears from the annexures of the Writ Petition (Page 20-43) that as per section 12 sub-section (3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain the bank published the auction sale notices in the Daily National Newspaper namely Dainik Prothom Alo on 14-6-2006 and also in a local newspaper, namely, Daily Azadhi on 14-6-2006 for selling the mortgaged property. It further appears that despite the aforesaid notices through newspapers the petitioner and others failed to appear in the Artha Rin Suit being No. 66 of 2006 filed on 07-9-2006 for realization of Tk. 53, 15, 235.76, and the said Suit was decreed exparte on 20-6-2007. The bank thereafter filed an Artha Execution case being . Artha Jari Case No. 153 of 2007. In the said Execution Case the learned judge of the Adalat by its orders directed to the plaintiff decree holder bank to the publish notices of auction sale in the Daily Newspapers. On the basis of the said orders the present respondent No. 2, as plaintiff, published auction sale notices in the National Daily Naya Diganta and the local newspaper Ajker Chattagram on 26-11-2007. Thereafter pursuant to the order of the Court plaintiff decree holder Bank published notices in the National newspapers of Ittefaque on 12-2-2008. It also appears from the order No. 8 dated 20-6-2008 that the debtors filed their Okalatnama in the Court to contest the Suit and filed an application for staying the auction proceedings until disposal of the writ petition No. 6552 of 2006. It also appear that the learned Adalat in the Execution Case by order No. 19 dated 03-3-2008 passed an order that the auction sale notice is also published in the National Daily Newspaper "Diganta" on 11-5-2008 and also National Daily "Shomokal" on 10-5-2008. Now a question is remained to be answered whether those publications of notices for auction sale of the properties of the petitioner as being a defaulter to repay the amount of loan is sufficient or not under the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003. In this regard section 7, section 12, sub-section (8) of section 19, sub-section (2) of section 13 and section 33 are relevant for the present purposes.

24. Firstly as to the service of sumons the provisions are stated in section 7 of the Ain which reads as follows :

“সমন জারী সম্পর্কিত বিধান ।- (১) আপাতত: বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, বাদী আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক এবং প্রাপ্তি স্বীকারসহ রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ডাকযোগে প্রেরণের নিমিত্ত, আরজির সহিত সমন জারীর জন্য সমুদয় তলবানা আদালতে দাখিল করিবেন এবং আদালত অবিলম্বে উহাদের একযোগে জারীর ব্যবস্থা করিবেন এবং যদি সমন ইস্যুর ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে জারী হইয়া ফেরত না আসে অথবা তৎপূর্বেই বিনা জারীতে ফেরত আসে, তাহা হইলে আদালত উহার পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে বাদীর খরচায় যে কোন একটি বহুল প্রচারিত বাংলা জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায় এবং তদুপরি একটি স্থানীয় পত্রিকায় যদি থাকে এবং আদালত যদি ন্যায় বিচারের স্বার্থে প্রয়োজনীয় মনে করে বিজ্ঞাপন প্রকাশের মাধ্যমে সমন জারী করাইবেন এবং অনুরুপ জারী আইনানুগ জারী মর্মে গণ্য হইবে।

(২) উপ-ধারা (১) এর বিধান এর অতিরিক্ত হিসাবে বাদী যদি নিজ খরচায় কোন সমন ও নোটিশ বিবাদীর উপর জারী করাইতে ইচ্ছা করেন, তাহা হইলে আদালত পূর্ববর্তী উপধারায় আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক সমন জারীকরনের প্রথমোক্ত ব্যবস্থাটির অতিরিক্ত এই ব্যবস্থাটিও কার্যকর করিবে।

(৩) জাতীয় দৈনিক পত্রিকায় বিজ্ঞাপন প্রকাশের মাধ্যমে সমন জারীর আগাম ব্যবস্থা হিসাবে বাদী আরজি দাখিলের সময় আদালতে আরজির সহিত একটি নমুনা বিজ্ঞাপন দাখিল করিবেন এবং আদালত পূর্ববর্তী উপ-ধারার বিধান অনুযায়ী করনীয় হইলে উক্ত বিজ্ঞাপনটি প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধন বা পরিবর্তন সাপেক্ষে তাৎক্ষণিকভাবে জারীকরণের নিমিত্ত প্রয়োজনীয় ব্যবস্থা করিবেন।

(৪) ২০০৩ সনের ৮ নং আইনের ধারা ৭ এর সংশোধন।

-উক্ত আইনের ধারা ৭ এর-

(ক) উপ-ধারা (১) এর পরিবর্তে নিম্নরুপ উপ-ধারা (১) প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে, যথা –

“(১) আপাতত: বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন বাদী আদালতের জারীকারক কর্তৃক প্রাপ্তি স্বীকার সহ রেজিষ্ট্রিকৃত ডাকযোগে প্রেরনের নিমিত্ত আরজির সহিত সমন জারীর জন্য সমুদয় তলবানা আদালতে দাখিল করিবেন এবং আদালত অবিলম্বে উহাদের একযোগে জারীর ব্যবস্থা করিবে এবং যদি সমন ইস্যুর ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে জারী হইয়া ফেরত না আসে অথবা তৎপূর্বেই বিনা জারীতে ফেরত আসে তাহা হইলে আদালত উহার পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) কার্যদিবসের মধ্যে Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 Order 5 এর rule 20 এর বিধান অনুযায়ী সমন জারী করাইবে।”

(খ) উপ-ধারা (৩) বিলুপ্ত হইবে।”

25. From the above provisions of law it appears that there are many ways of service of notices which have been described in section 7 that including registered post with AD and alternatively, publication of notices through well published National Bengali Newspaper along with publication of notices in a local Newspaper and such notification would be consider as sufficient service of notice upon the party.

26. In the present case an exparte decree was passed on after serving required notices by post to the parties and also after publishing auction sale notice in the newspaper under Ain 20-6-2007 but the present petitioner filed an application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain on 25-9-2008 by way of a Misc case alleging that she started to live at Dhaka. Therefore, she did not have any knowledge of the decree before 1 8-9-2008. From the discussions in the aforesaid paragraphs as to the publication of auction sale notices in the newspapers on several occasions can be considered as sufficient notice under the Ain. As to the Power of Attorney containing a ratification clause executed by the present petitioner on 10-10-2000 in favour of the present respondent No.5 who contested the Execution case and also filed several writ petitions challenging the different orders passed by the Adalat at different time. As an attorney of the petitioner the respondent No.5 was fully aware about the proceeding filed by the bank by way of Artha Rin Suit and also Artha Jari Case, in such a given fact, would it not be sufficient knowledge on the part of the petitioner through her constituted Attorney appointed by a registered document which is still seem to be a valid piece of document. Moreover, the publication by way of the public advertisement as to sale of the property of the respondent No.5 for himself and on behalf of the present petitioner can be taken to have sufficient knowledge of the proceedings which were going on against the respondent No.5 to 10 and also against the present petitioner.

27. Despite the above, there is another dilemma needs to be resolved in the present case which is that the loan was obtained by the petitioner through executing a Power of Attorney in favour of the respondent No.5, Md. Saidur Rahman but the present application under section 19 was filed by the petitioner through another Special Power of Attorney authorizing one Shahidul Islam Son of Alhaz Aslamudden without cancelling the valid existing Power of Attorney authorizing to borrow, to mortgage, to sell, look after her property. We do not have any information from the record or from the petitioner's learned Advocate when this Power of Attorney to file this application under section 19 of the Artha Rin Ain was executed or why the petitioner executed a new Power of Attorney when she was aware that she had a valid Power of Attorney. On the basis of the aforesaid application by its order the learned Artha Rin Adalat, Chittagong passed the impugned order on 07-10-2008 disbelieving the facts of knowledge on the part of petitioner for filing this application. The learned Adalat also found that the mortgage property was sold in auction to the auction purchaser and a transfer deed was executed creating rights of the auction purchaser, the respondent No. 11, who has already paid up all the purchase money. In this stage of case the learned Adalat has rightly disbelieved as to the knowledge of the decree and the device of filing this case by the petitioner.

28. Now before we go to deal with the application under section 19 filed by the petitioner it would be convenient to reproduce section 19 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 which reads as follows:

১৯। “একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কিত বিধান।– (১) মামলার শুনানীর জন্য ধার্য কোন তারিখে বিবাদী আদালতে অনুপস্থিত থাকিলে কিংবা মামলা শুনানীর জন্য গৃহীত হইবার পর ডাকিয়া বিবাদীকে উপস্থিত পাওয়া না গেলে আদালত মামলা একতরফা সুত্রে নিষ্পত্তি করিবে।

(২) কোন মামলা একতরফা সুত্রে ডিক্রী হইলে বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রির তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রি রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন।

(৩) উপ-ধারা (২) এর বিধান অনুযায়ী দরখাস্ত দাখিলের ক্ষেত্রে বিবাদীকে উক্ত দরখাস্ত দাখিলের তারিখের পরবর্তী ১৫ (পনের) দিবসের মধ্যে ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমানের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরুপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে অথবা জামানত স্বরুপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট পে অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিময় দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে হইবে।

(৪) উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধানমতে ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা জমাদানের সংগে সংগে দরখাস্তটি মঞ্জুর হইবে, একতরফা ডিক্রি রদ হইবে এবং মূল মামলা উহার পূর্বের নম্বর ও নথিতে পুনরুজ্জীবিত হইবে এবং আদালতে ঐ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে; এবং অতঃপর মামলাটি যে পর্যায়ে একতরফা নিষ্পত্তি হইয়াছিল ঐ পর্যায়ের অব্যবহিত পূর্ববর্তী পর্যায় হইতে পরিচালিত হইবে।

(৫) বিবাদী উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান মতে ডিক্রিকৃত অর্থের ১০% এর সমপরিমান টাকা বাদীর দাবীর সেই পরিমানের জন্য স্বীকৃতিস্বরুপ নগদ সংশ্লিষ্ট আর্থিক প্রতিষ্ঠানে অথবা জামানত স্বরুপ ব্যাংক ড্রাফট, পে-অর্ডার বা অন্য কোন প্রকার নগদায়নযোগ্য বিনিময়ে দলিল (Negotiable Instrument) আকারে জামানত হিসাবে আদালতে জমাদান করিতে ব্যর্থ হইলে উক্ত দরখাস্তটি সরাসরি খারিজ হইবে এবং আদালতে ঐ মর্মে একটি আদেশ লিপিবদ্ধ করিবে।

(৬) অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন মামলা, বাদীর অনুপস্থিতির বা ব্যর্থতা হেতু খারিজ করা যাইবে না এবং এইরুপ ক্ষেত্রে আদালত নথিতে উপস্থাপিত কাগজাদি পরীক্ষা করিয়িা গুনাগুণ বিশ্লেষণে মামলা নিষ্পত্তি করিবে।

২০। অর্থ ঋণ আদালতের আদেশের চুড়ান্ততা ।- এই আইনের বিধান ব্যতিরেকে কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট অর্থ ঋণ আদালতে বিচারাধীন কোন কার্যধারা বা উহার কোন আদেশ রায় বা ডিক্রির বিষয়ে কোন প্রশ্ন উত্থাপন করা যাইবে না এবং এই আইনের বিধানকে উপেক্ষা করিয়া কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষের নিকট আবেদন করিয়া কোন প্রতিকার দাবী বা প্রার্থনা করা হইলে ঐরুপ আবেদন কোন আদালত বা কর্তৃপক্ষ গ্রাহ্য করিবে না।”

29. From the above provisions of law, the petitioner had a remedy provided under section 19 but the requirement under sub-section (2) of section 19 is important for the present purposes which reads as follows:

“কোন মামলা একতরফা সুত্রে ডিক্রি হইলে বিবাদী উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রির তারিখের অথবা উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী সম্পর্কে অবগত হইবার ৩০ (ত্রিশ) দিবসের মধ্যে উপ-ধারা (৩) এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে উক্ত একতরফা ডিক্রী রদের জন্য দরখাস্ত করিতে পারিবেন।”

<u>30. The petitioner can only get any relief under above provisions of law if and only if, the petitioner did not have any knowledge as to the exparte decree passed on 20-6-2007 or as to the Jari Case being No. 159 of 2007 even prior to 18-9-2008. From the above discussion as to either by herself or through her constituted attorney would be sufficient for knowledge of the case which have given her to file an application under sub-section (2) within 30 days period of time from knowledge for filing an application for setting aside the exparte decree but in the present case we are not satisfied that the petitioner did not have knowledge from the date of decree dated 20-6-2007 to 18-9-2008. In the above circumstances we do not find that the learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Chittagong committed any error of law by passing the impugned order dated 07-10-2008.</u>

31. Regarding the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in relation that the Court can interfere into an order of the Court below if it is an error apparent on the face of record, but after examining the impugned order, we found that the order is passed with conformity of the evidence in record and the information available in the record of the case.

32. Regarding the submissions made by the learned Advocate about the publication of notice for auction sale in the National newspaper which should be among the top ten newspapers. We have examined the record and mentioned in our discussions above that the original notices for auction sale were published in the Daily National Newspapers, Namely, Dainik Ittafaque, Dainik Prothom Alo and Daily Azadi Chattagram, Agrabad and subsequently in the execution case there are many publication of auction sale notices through National Newspapers like Ittefaque, Samokal and Naya Diganta which are within the ten well published top ten newspapers in the country, therefore, the aforesaid decision of our apex Court has no application in the present case.

33. In view of the above, we do not consider that it would not be justified for any party to interfere the Court proceedings on the basis of a false and mistaken plea in order to mislead the Court to get an unfair benefit out of this Court. From the given facts of the case it appears to us that the auction purchaser respondent No. 11 paid value of the auction property and obtained a sell certificate from the Court which has also been registered in the mean time.

34. In view of the above, we do not find any merit in the Rule.

35. In the result, the Rule discharged without any order as to cost.

36. The interim order passed hereby stands vacated.

The office is directed to communicate the order to the respondent No. 1, the Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Chittagong at once.

End.
